text:
incident-bot: ALERT: reserved pool 'resv-prod-01' at 100% GPU utilization; sustained queue growth detected. queue_length=312, p99_latency=2.1s. autoscaler health: ERROR (scale_attempts=3, last_attempt=30m ago). paging oncall. :rotating_light:
ryan_oncall: I'm on it. pinging SRE and runtime. any initial customer impact visible?
marta_p: seeing throttles for several enterprise tenants in resv-prod-01. acme-health showing request rejections (429) and long queue times. logs show many long-lived sessions from a single tenant session-id prefix: "acme-wn-".
devon_m: adding context: autoscaler failed on backoff due to recent rate limit from cloud-provider API — 429 on scale-up call. it retried and hit limit, scaled only 0->0 (no new nodes).
kyle_ops: confirmed cloud autoscale throttle. provider returned error: "RateLimitExceeded: Scale operations exceeded". we have burst capacity quota available in region eu-west-1 but it requires manual request to bump for the reserved pool's instance profile.
sophie_support: Acme support channel reports degraded responses for their scheduled batch jobs starting ~06:12 UTC. Nora from Acme in call now. @ajay_account on the bridge?
ajay_account: joining bridge, pinged acme contacts. they report 40% of generations failing and several timeouts. customers on Dedicated expect reserved capacity, so high priority.
nora_acme: (via bridge) seeing user-facing errors in our roster upload flow. our job retries thrash the queue. please advise ETA.
ryan_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) apply temporary per-tenant concurrency cap for noisy tenant (acme-health) to free up slots; 2) enable burst fallback to shared-hosted tier for affected routes; 3) continue escalations with cloud provider for autoscale quota. who's taking which?
marta_p: I can push per-tenant cap via routing policy; will set max_concurrency=16 for tenant acme-health on resv-prod-01 routes. doing now.
(dev console) marta_p: applied policy change: 
```
route_policy {
  match: tenant=="acme-health"
  action: throttle_concurrency(max=16)
}
```
(reacts: :white_check_mark:)
devon_m: I'll enable fallback routing to hosted-burst for compatible model variants; adding soft-failover so that if dedicated pool enqueues >200 we'll route to hosted with map of model compatibility. pushing config now.
(dev console) devon_m: config snippet:
```
fallback_policy {
  condition: queue_length > 200
  target: hosted-burst
  strategy: prefer-compatible-quantized
}
```
(reacts: :rocket:)
kyle_ops: I'm opening a ticket with cloud provider and escalating to their capacity team. created ticket CP-91234, link: https://cloud.example/cases/CP-91234. also submitting manual quota bump request for the resv instance profile. ETA from provider uncertain.
ryan_oncall: rolling mitigation timeline: 1) throttle noisy tenant - done? 2) fallback routing - done? 3) short-term customer communication - @sophie_support draft? 4) long-term: restore autoscaler and recover pool capacity.
sophie_support: drafting message for Acme: "We're seeing elevated throttling in your reserved pool due to noisy sessions; we've applied short-term limits and are routing excess traffic to fallback capacity. Expect gradual recovery over next 15-30 minutes. We'll keep you posted." sending to @nora_acme for ack.
nora_acme: thanks, that's useful. we can delay remaining batches for 30min. will monitor.
marta_p: monitoring metrics after throttle: queue_length dropped from 312 -> 78 within 4m. p99 latency improved to 1.1s. throttled ~120 concurrent sessions for acme-health.
devon_m: fallback routes are seeing traffic now; hosted-burst handling ~60 connections. logs show model variant compatibility OK, minor tokenization mismatches on one internal prompt — no major user-facing regressions.
kyle_ops: cloud provider responded to ticket: temporary increase approved but needs infra change window (15m) to attach extra nodes. I can run the attach now if we want to expand resv pool. advise?
ryan_oncall: let's attach +2 nodes to resv-prod-01, but only after ensuring autoscaler backoff won't immediately try another scale action (we'll disable autoscaler until we stabilize).
devon_m: disabling autoscaler for resv-prod-01 and applying manual scale +2. command: `infractl pools scale resv-prod-01 --delta 2 --manual`
(dev console) devon_m: autoscaler disabled. manual scale started. watch for cloud attach logs.
kyle_ops: attach completed. GPUs added and health OK. pool utilization now 78%. queue_length 46 and falling.
marta_p: re-checking logs for noisy session origins — looks like a runaway retry loop from an older SDK version in acme's integration. flagged to acme engineering.
sophie_support: notified Acme with update, they accepted backlog pause and are validating SDK update path.
ajay_account: telling the customer we'll coordinate a postmortem and recommended a prompt-level rate limit to prevent future noisy bursts.
ryan_oncall: follow-ups: - exfiltrate exact offending session IDs and create support ticket with Acme engineering (assigned to @sophie_support). - re-enable autoscaler with safe cooldown and provider rate-limit backoff handling (devon). - add server-side detection for long-lived sessions >45m (marta). - schedule post-incident review and P0 blameless postmortem.
marta_p: creating an alert rule to detect tenant-dominant queues (>40% of queue from single tenant) and auto-action to cap concurrency.
devon_m: plan to change autoscaler client to exponential backoff with jitter and circuit-breaker to avoid provider 429 loops. will review with infra team tomorrow.
kyle_ops: cloud provider follow-up: they recommended using a single larger instance type instead of several small attaches to reduce API calls for scale. will prototype.
sophie_support: Acme confirmed SDK fix on their side and will monitor next scheduled job. they want a postmortem and timeline.
ryan_oncall: marking incident as mitigated for now. creating incident channel #incident-4491234567 for postmortem. thanks all, great coordination. :tada:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status changed -> mitigation_in_progress -> mitigated at 4491240321. postmortem required.
